Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Draft review — 3 stars

Three stars. Some genuinely great work in my grooming van, but the way a plumbing failure was handled made this a much more frustrating experience than it needed to be.

I’m a mobile dog groomer in Halifax, and Harbourline fitted out my Transit in August. First, credit where it’s due: the stainless tub and ramp are honestly the best thing about the van. The dogs walk right in, which makes my working day easier and their day less of a production. I use that setup constantly and I’m really happy with it.

Unfortunately, on October 27, a fitting on the hot-water line let go in the middle of a groom. Water went across the floor and into the cabinet, and I had to towel off my client’s dog and send him home half finished.

The dog in question was Moose, a 110 lb Bernese, who sat in the tub through the whole flood like a king surveying his waterfront property. Absolutely unbothered. I was the one screaming. Moose apparently booked a spa day with an unexpected water feature and saw no reason to complain.

I cancelled the rest of that day, then six more bookings while waiting to get the van in. It was off the road from October 27 to November 6. For a business that literally needs its wheels and hot water to work, that was a pretty rough stretch.

The leak itself isn’t what upset me most. Things break. Even good work can have a problem, and I wasn’t expecting a van that would never need a repair.

What bothered me was the response before anyone had inspected it. Glenn’s first email said these lines don’t just let go and suggested the heater had been run dry or someone had been hanging things off the pipe. He said that would be user error and wouldn’t be covered. Neither had happened, and the pipe was behind a cabinet door. The earliest appointment offered was November 3, with a $180 diagnostic fee.

Being told it was likely something I’d done, while standing there with a flooded workspace and a calendar full of cancellations, did not go over brilliantly.

To Glenn’s credit, he did own it in the end. When the van was ready on November 6, he explained that his supplier had substituted a cheaper compression fitting on the outlet, said that was on them, and replaced all the fittings on the hot side. He also removed the $180 charge. That matters, and it’s only fair to include it.

So this isn’t a “everything was terrible” review. The tub and ramp are great, the problem was eventually acknowledged, and the fittings were replaced. But the downtime and the initial assumption of user error took a lot of the shine off the experience.

My advice to other groomers or trades considering a fitout: get the warranty details in writing, including how diagnostic charges and possible workmanship issues will be handled. My invoice included a 12-month workmanship warranty excluding misuse or user error; I wish we’d clarified the process before I needed it.

Good parts of the build, a disappointing repair experience, and a better ending than beginning. Three stars feels fair. Moose would probably give the pool party five, but he doesn’t manage the bookings.
